final.decision_summary:
The top 10 follows the Borda aggregate of the three judges (quality, practicality, coverage), with one forced swap. Ranks 1 to 9 are Borda ranks 1 to 9: Qwen3.8-27B (29 points), Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (27), K2 Horizon MoVA 36B A4B (24), K2 Horizon 7B (20), Gemma 4 26B-A4B (16), Qwen3-Coder-Next (15), Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B (15), Groot-19B-A3B-261023 (5) and gpt-oss-20b (5). Ties are kept in the order the aggregate lists them. Borda rank 10 was Nanbeige4.3-33B (3 points, quality judge only, tied with Gemma 4 12B). That left out the DeepSeek family, which the user requires, so DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B (1 point) takes rank 10. It is labelled chat and reasoning only: it has no tool calling and is not for OpenCode agent mode. Nanbeige moves to honorable mentions as a trial candidate. The other required families are covered: Qwen (1, 2, 6), Gemma (5), Nemotron (7, Bolt now replaces Lightning as the best Nemotron), gpt-oss (9).

Runtime: llama.cpp ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-cuda-b12407 (CUDA 12.8.1) is the primary runtime for all ten. Every llama.cpp command on this laptop needs docker -e GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1 placed before the image name (#27330 reproduced on driver 595.99.02); after the image, llama-server parses -e as --escape and refuses to start. Use -np 1 and --jinja. Avoid server-cuda13-b12407 because its NVIDIA_REQUIRE_CUDA is cuda>=13.5 while driver 595.99.02 offers CUDA 13.2, so the container is likely refused (inferred); #28581 is not the reason. --n-cpu-moe N moves the experts of blocks 0 to N-1 to system RAM and counts all blocks, not only MoE layers. vLLM v0.33.0 is a secondary path only: for gpt-oss-20b at 64k (needs --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95, --kv-cache-dtype fp8 and --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN) and for Groot NVFP4 with --language-model-only. None of the four highest-ranked models fits vLLM's 14.65 GiB budget, and vLLM expert offload is undone for Marlin weights (#66264).

The new picks rest on independent Artificial Analysis data (MoVA TB2.1 56.6 / tau3 32.0, K2 7B 44.2 / 27.6) or on vendor data only (Bolt: NVIDIA's own table; Groot: self-reported, anonymous publisher). Every context and speed figure is an estimate from source-backed arithmetic. Nothing has run on this machine. The NVIDIA Container Toolkit with CDI must be installed first, and each pick needs a /v1/models check plus an OpenCode tool-call smoke test before use. I rechecked the load-bearing GGUF sizes live on 2026-11-15 through the HF tree API (MoVA Q4_K_M 21.14, K2 7B Q8_0 8.92 / Q5_K_M 6.39, Bolt 20.51 plus 1.61 GiB mmproj, Groot Q4_K_M 10.86 GiB). I also confirmed the sampling recommendations in the raw README of each new pick.

top10.est_context: Estimate: 65536 with q8_0 KV. KV = 2 x 36 x 8 x 128 x 2 B = 144 KiB/token f16, about 76.5 KiB q8_0, so 4.78 GiB at 64k. 8.11 + 4.78 + 0.8 = 13.7 GiB. f16 KV at 64k (17.9 GiB) does not fit.
top10.thinking: Always on. There is no official off switch; Ollama's think flag is the only toggle.
top10.tool_calling: No. The template never renders tools, vLLM's deepseek_v3 parser raises at init, and AA measured tau2 0%.
top10.parsers_or_flags: docker run ... -e GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1 ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-cuda-b12407 -hf unsloth/DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B-GGUF:Q8_0 -c 65536 -ngl 99 -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 -fa on -np 1 --reasoning-format deepseek. Do not set capabilities.tools in OpenCode.
